item.title: Rising CO2 levels linked to shifts in human blood chemistry
item.description:
Researchers found that increasing atmospheric carbon dioxide correlates with rising bicarbonate levels and declining calcium and phosphorus in human blood. This trend was identified through an analysis of over two decades of U.S. health data.

item.title: Lack of fiber causes gut microbes to consume mucus
item.description:
When dietary fiber is limited, gut microbes may begin consuming proteins from the protective mucus lining. Researchers found that fiber prevents this process and helps produce beneficial compounds.

item.title: New Mosasaur Bones Discovered in 30-Year-Old Japanese Fossils
item.description:
Re-examination of fossils from Osaka has revealed previously unrecognized bones from a giant Cretaceous mosasaur. The unique anatomical features suggest the remains may belong to an entirely new species.

item.title: Food preservative linked to rising youth suicide deaths
item.description:
A common food-preservation chemical is being linked to increasing suicide rates among young people and men in the UK. Researchers suggest the impact may be underestimated and are calling for urgent restrictions on access.

item.title: New study challenges long-held theory on social insect evolution
item.description:
A massive new analysis suggests genetics alone may not explain the complex social colonies of ants, bees, and wasps. Researchers believe other unique insect traits may play a more significant role in their evolution.

item.title: Brain receptor mechanism for weight loss discovered
item.description:
Researchers found how targeting the GIP receptor in different brain regions promotes weight loss. This discovery explains why diverse obesity drugs yield similar results and suggests potential benefits for combining GIP and GLP-1 treatments.

item.title: The need for objective answers on Covid-19 origins
item.description:

item.description:
